newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone coup leaders defiant against Nigerians.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone coup leaders defiant against Nigerians.

text.p: Sierra Leone coup leaders told Nigerian negotiators on Thursday they refused to jeopardise the new alliance between the army and rebels by restoring the ousted civilian government of Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.

"We are not prepared to hand over to former president Kabbah. If president Kabbah takes over again, he will jeopardise the peace that we have been able to achieve with the RUF rebels," Sierra Leone's chief of defence staff Brigadier Samuel Koroma told reporters.
Koroma said they had been unable to reach any agreement with a delegation sent by Nigerian military leader General Sani Abacha which arrived on Wednesday.

"We have sent a message to the Nigerian head of state through the Nigerian delegation which arrived yesterday in Freetown, saying that General Abacha must choose between peace in Sierra Leone or the forced return of President Kabbah to power by Nigeria and ECOMOG," Koroma said.
Nigeria, which already had troops of the West African ECOMOG force in Freetown under a defence agreement, has been steadily reinforcing in the city since the May 25 coup.
Nigerian gunboats shelled the capital on Monday in a show of force. Rebels responded by attacking Nigerian troops guarding foreigners at a hotel.
